allii-arrange-figures.title: Set out the clay figures
allii-arrange-figures.description: Clay figures and tongue-shaped pieces are placed for the counter-ritual.

allii-seat-patient.title: Seat the patient toward the Sun-god
allii-seat-patient.description: The bewitched person sits facing the Sun-god.

allii-raise-vessel.title: Raise the vessel and figures
allii-raise-vessel.description: The Old Woman lifts a naktamu vessel together with the clay figures toward the Sun-god.

allii-return-address.title: Demand that the sorcery return
allii-return-address.description: The address to the Sun-god asks that the maker of the bewitchment carry it away.

allii-wind-wool.title: Wind coloured wool around the figures
allii-wind-wool.description: The Old Woman winds wool thread around the figures while naming the affliction she is returning.

allii-set-basket.title: Place the deposit beneath the bed
allii-set-basket.description: A prepared deposit of objects is set under the patient's bed.

allii-sleep-over.title: Sleep over the deposit
allii-sleep-over.description: The patient sleeps over the placed ritual objects.

allii-lift-at-dawn.title: Lift the deposit at daybreak
allii-lift-at-dawn.description: At first light, the Old Woman removes the bedside deposit and moves it over the patient.

allii-press-earth.title: Press earth against the patient
allii-press-earth.description: The Old Woman presses an earth clod against the patient while uttering a purification analogy.

allii-press-dough.title: Press dough against the patient
allii-press-dough.description: The Old Woman presses a lump of dough against the patient and speaks a life-giving analogy.

uhhamuwa-bring-ram.title: Bring a ram
uhhamuwa-bring-ram.description: A ram is driven up for the rite.

uhhamuwa-twist-wool.title: Twist the coloured wool
uhhamuwa-twist-wool.description: Blue, red, yellow-green, black and white wool are combined.

uhhamuwa-make-wreath.title: Make a wool wreath
uhhamuwa-make-wreath.description: The combined wool is made into a wreath or ring.

uhhamuwa-crown-ram.title: Adorn the ram
uhhamuwa-crown-ram.description: The wool wreath is placed on one ram.

uhhamuwa-lead-to-road.title: Lead the ram toward the enemy road
uhhamuwa-lead-to-road.description: The adorned ram is driven onto the road toward enemy territory.

uhhamuwa-appeal-over-ram.title: Address the hostile god
uhhamuwa-appeal-over-ram.description: An appeal presents the adorned ram and asks the god to be at peace with Ḫatti.

uhhamuwa-drive-away-ram.title: Drive the ram away
uhhamuwa-drive-away-ram.description: The crowned ram is sent into enemy territory.

uhhamuwa-bring-fodder-fat.title: Bring fodder for divine horses
uhhamuwa-bring-fodder-fat.description: Fodder and other named materials are brought for the god’s horses and attendants.
uhhamuwa-bring-fodder-fat.matchRule: Bring fodder for a divine team of horses. Keep accompanying fat, straw or wool and the named recipient on each source occurrence; later feeding and speech remain separate acts.

uhhamuwa-address-horses-chariot.title: Address the god about his horses
uhhamuwa-address-horses-chariot.description: The speech asks that the horses eat, the chariot be greased, and the god turn back toward his land.

uhhamuwa-bring-goat-sheep.title: Bring a goat and two sheep
uhhamuwa-bring-goat-sheep.description: A billy goat and two sheep are brought into the rite.

offer-goat.title: Offer a goat
offer-goat.description: Assign a goat to a deity as an offering.
offer-goat.matchRule: The named recipient differs between rituals; the shared task is offering a goat.

offer-sheep-to-sun-god.title: Offer a sheep to the Sun-god
offer-sheep-to-sun-god.description: Assign a sheep or ewe to the Sun-god.
offer-sheep-to-sun-god.matchRule: Both passages specify a sheep or ewe offered to the Sun-god.

slaughter-sheep.title: Slaughter sheep
slaughter-sheep.description: The prescribed killing of sheep or rams before cooking them.
slaughter-sheep.matchRule: Both texts prescribe slaughter of sheep. Ašḫella also slaughters goats.

cook-sheep-meat.title: Cook sheep meat
cook-sheep-meat.description: Cook flesh from the sheep slaughtered in the rite.
cook-sheep-meat.matchRule: The shared action is cooking sheep meat after slaughter.

uhhamuwa-bring-food-drink.title: Bring food and drink
uhhamuwa-bring-food-drink.description: Cheese, sour bread, wine, beer and fruit are brought, along with named vessels.

uhhamuwa-prepare-for-road-god.title: Prepare them for the road god
uhhamuwa-prepare-for-road-god.description: The gathered provisions are prepared for the god of the road.

ashella-prepare-ram.title: Prepare a ram
ashella-prepare-ram.description: Each army lord supplies a ram at dusk.

ashella-twist-wool.title: Twist three colours of wool
ashella-twist-wool.description: White, red and green wool are worked into a cord.

ashella-bind-ram.title: Bind the cord and rings to the ram
ashella-bind-ram.description: The cord and metal ornaments are fastened to the ram’s neck and horns.

ashella-tether-ram.title: Tether the ram before a tent
ashella-tether-ram.description: The adorned ram is tied in front of a tent for the night.

ashella-appeal.title: Ask the plague god to be appeased
ashella-appeal.description: The speaker asks the god responsible for the plague to accept the tethered rams.

ashella-release-rams.title: Release the rams at the enemy border
ashella-release-rams.description: The rams are led through camp and let loose at the enemy border.

ashella-wash-salt-water.title: Wash hands in salted water
ashella-wash-salt-water.description: Salt is mixed with water, and the participants wash their hands.

ashella-pass-between-fires.title: Pass between two fires
ashella-pass-between-fires.description: Two fires are lit, and the participants walk between them.

ashella-bring-pig.title: Bring a pig on the third day
ashella-bring-pig.description: A pig is driven to a different open place with a goat and ram.

ashella-offer-pig.title: Offer the pig to the plague god
ashella-offer-pig.description: The pig is offered with the goat and ram to the god responsible for the plague.

ashella-offer-bull.title: Offer a bull to the Storm-god
ashella-offer-bull.description: The bull is offered to the Storm-god.

ashella-offer-rams.title: Offer three sheep to all the gods
ashella-offer-rams.description: Three sheep are offered to all the gods.

pulisa-select-substitutes.title: Select a prisoner and a woman
pulisa-select-substitutes.description: A prisoner of war and a woman from the enemy land are chosen as substitutes.

pulisa-remove-king-garments.title: Remove the king’s festive clothes
pulisa-remove-king-garments.description: The king takes off his festive garments.

pulisa-dress-man.title: Clothe the man in the king’s garments
pulisa-dress-man.description: The prisoner receives the king’s festive garments.

pulisa-dress-woman.title: Clothe the woman in festive garments
pulisa-dress-woman.description: The woman is dressed in festive garments.

pulisa-address-man.title: Address the male deity
pulisa-address-man.description: The speaker offers the adorned man as a substitute and asks that he carry the plague away.

pulisa-address-woman.title: Address the female deity
pulisa-address-woman.description: The corresponding words are spoken to the woman concerning a female deity.

pulisa-bring-bull-ewe.title: Bring a bull and ewe
pulisa-bring-bull-ewe.description: A bull and ewe from the enemy land are brought forward.

pulisa-ring-bull.title: Fit rings at the bull’s ears
pulisa-ring-bull.description: The bull is fitted with ašuša-objects at its ears; their identification as rings is uncertain.

pulisa-draw-wool.title: Draw coloured wool from the king’s mouth
pulisa-draw-wool.description: Red, green, black and partly restored white wool are drawn out of the king’s mouth.

pulisa-address-bull.title: Offer the bull to the male deity
pulisa-address-bull.description: The speaker offers the bull as a substitute and asks it to carry the plague away.

pulisa-address-ewe.title: Offer the ewe to the female deity
pulisa-address-ewe.description: The ewe is brought forward and the corresponding words address a female deity.

pulisa-send-animals-ahead.title: Drive the bull and ewe ahead
pulisa-send-animals-ahead.description: The bull and ewe are driven in front of the two human substitutes.

tunnawiya-prepare-black-animals.title: Bring the black animals
tunnawiya-prepare-black-animals.description: A black sheep, piglet and puppy are prepared; the prescribed sexes depend on the patient.

tunnawiya-set-out-black-clothes.title: Set out the black clothes
tunnawiya-set-out-black-clothes.description: Black clothing, shoes and wool are supplied for the patient.

tunnawiya-offer-bread-wine.title: Offer bread and wine
tunnawiya-offer-bread-wine.description: Thin bread, groats and wine are offered at the riverbank or spring.
tunnawiya-offer-bread-wine.matchRule: Break thin bread and pour wine at a water source; the riverbank and spring remain distinct occurrences.

tunnawiya-address-riverbank-goddess.title: Address the riverbank Mother-goddess
tunnawiya-address-riverbank-goddess.description: Tunnawiya asks the riverbank Mother-goddess to cleanse the patient with clay.

tunnawiya-collect-clay.title: Take clay from a water source
tunnawiya-collect-clay.description: Tunnawiya takes clay first from the riverbank and then from the spring.
tunnawiya-collect-clay.matchRule: Take clay from a named water source; preserve riverbank and spring as distinct locations on the occurrences.

tunnawiya-build-reed-hut.title: Build the reed shelter
tunnawiya-build-reed-hut.description: A reed shelter is built beside the river, away from tilled land.

tunnawiya-make-clay-figures.title: Make clay tongues and oxen
tunnawiya-make-clay-figures.description: Tunnawiya models twelve tongue shapes and two oxen from the collected clay.

tunnawiya-dress-in-black.title: Dress the patient in black
tunnawiya-dress-in-black.description: At first light the patient puts on the black clothes.

tunnawiya-hold-black-sheep.title: Hold a black sheep over the patient
tunnawiya-hold-black-sheep.description: Tunnawiya holds a black sheep over the patient while reciting.
tunnawiya-hold-black-sheep.matchRule: A sheep is held over the patient so that it takes up the condition. KUB 7.53+ specifies a black sheep with a Luwian incantation; KUB 9.34 §20 holds a sheep over the chest without naming its colour. Other animals held over the patient (piglet, puppy) are separate tasks.

tunnawiya-hold-piglet.title: Hold the piglet over the patient
tunnawiya-hold-piglet.description: A piglet is held over the patient with its own incantation.

tunnawiya-hold-puppy.title: Hold the puppy over the patient
tunnawiya-hold-puppy.description: A puppy is held over the patient with its own incantation.

tunnawiya-hold-clay-tongue.title: Hold a clay tongue over the patient
tunnawiya-hold-clay-tongue.description: A clay tongue is lifted over the patient with a prescribed incantation.

tunnawiya-melt-figures.title: Melt the wax and tallow figures
tunnawiya-melt-figures.description: After holding the figures over the patient, Tunnawiya melts them.

tunnawiya-wash-hands-wine.title: Wash the hands with wine
tunnawiya-wash-hands-wine.description: The patient rises and washes the hands with wine.

tunnawiya-wash-with-water.title: Wash oneself with water
tunnawiya-wash-with-water.description: The patient washes with water while Tunnawiya continues the incantation.

tunnawiya-remove-coloured-wool.title: Take blue and red wool off the patient
tunnawiya-remove-coloured-wool.description: Tunnawiya removes blue and red wool from the patient while speaking.

tunnawiya-strip-black-clothes.title: Slit the black shirt
tunnawiya-strip-black-clothes.description: Tunnawiya cuts the black shirt down its length and removes the dark garments.

tunnawiya-smash-empty-pot.title: Smash the empty pot
tunnawiya-smash-empty-pot.description: An empty pot is waved over the patient and smashed.

tunnawiya-bathe-over-figure.title: Bathe over a clay figure
tunnawiya-bathe-over-figure.description: A clay figure is placed beneath the patient’s feet as the patient bathes.

tunnawiya-comb-down.title: Comb the patient downward
tunnawiya-comb-down.description: Maidservants draw boxwood combs downward over the patient.

tunnawiya-release-into-river.title: Send the used objects into the river
tunnawiya-release-into-river.description: The combs, clothing and other used objects are sent into the river.

tunnawiya-burn-small-animals.title: Burn the piglet and puppy
tunnawiya-burn-small-animals.description: The puppy and piglet are taken to uncultivated ground and burned.

tunnawiya-pass-through-gate.title: Pass beneath the wooden gate
tunnawiya-pass-through-gate.description: The patient leaves beneath the alanza-wood gate as Tunnawiya speaks.

tunnawiya-take-cow-by-horn.title: Take the cow by its horn
tunnawiya-take-cow-by-horn.description: Tunnawiya takes hold of a cow by its horn to begin a fertility comparison.

tunnawiya-wish-for-offspring.title: Ask for offspring through the cow analogy
tunnawiya-wish-for-offspring.description: Addressing the Sun-god, Tunnawiya likens the patient’s hoped-for descendants to a fertile cow’s increase.

tunnawiya-touch-fruit-tree.title: Take hold of a fruit-bearing tree
tunnawiya-touch-fruit-tree.description: Tunnawiya takes hold of a fruit-bearing tree.

tunnawiya-wish-by-tree.title: Ask for descendants through the tree analogy
tunnawiya-wish-by-tree.description: Tunnawiya addresses the Sun-god and compares descendants to the fruit on a tree.

tunnawiya-libate-sun-god.title: Pour wine for the Sun-god
tunnawiya-libate-sun-god.description: The patient pours a libation and calls on the Sun-god to keep the cleansing effective.

tunnawiya-return-river-offering.title: Offer bread again at the riverbank
tunnawiya-return-river-offering.description: Tunnawiya returns to the riverbank with bread and groats.

dandanku-mix-fodder.title: Mix grain and straw
dandanku-mix-fodder.description: The grain and straw are combined as fodder.

dandanku-scatter-fodder.title: Scatter fodder on the road
dandanku-scatter-fodder.description: The mixture is scattered across the ḫaddari- of the road.

dandanku-address-grooms.title: Ask Iyarri’s grooms to feed the horses
dandanku-address-grooms.description: The speech directs Iyarri’s grooms to give the fodder to the horses.

dandanku-address-maids.title: Ask the god’s maids to take the wool
dandanku-address-maids.description: The speech directs divine maidservants to take the coloured wool.

dandanku-bring-three-animals.title: Bring a kid, piglet and puppy
dandanku-bring-three-animals.description: Three young animals are brought for the Seven.

dandanku-kill-three-animals.title: Cut apart the three animals
dandanku-kill-three-animals.description: The animals are cut apart for the Seven at an untouched place.

dandanku-libate-to-seven.title: Pour beer and wine for the Seven
dandanku-libate-to-seven.description: Beer and wine are poured three times to the Seven.

paskuwatti-arrange-provisions.title: Arrange bread, food, wine and clothes
paskuwatti-arrange-provisions.description: Food, wine, wool and the offerant’s clothes are arranged on soldier-bread.

paskuwatti-carry-offering.title: Carry the offerings into the open country
paskuwatti-carry-offering.description: A virgin girl lifts the offering and takes it to a fresh outdoor place.

paskuwatti-build-reed-gate.title: Make a gate of reeds
paskuwatti-build-reed-gate.description: Paškuwatti makes gates of reed in the open country.

paskuwatti-bind-gate.title: Bind the gate with red and white wool
paskuwatti-bind-gate.description: The reed gates are bound with coloured wool.

paskuwatti-give-spindle.title: Give the man a spindle and distaff
paskuwatti-give-spindle.description: The offerant receives the two implements before passing beneath the gate.

paskuwatti-pass-gate.title: Pass beneath the gate
paskuwatti-pass-gate.description: The offerant passes beneath the reed gate while holding the implements.
paskuwatti-pass-gate.matchRule: Passing under a constructed ritual threshold; material and purpose stay with each occurrence.

paskuwatti-exchange-implements.title: Exchange spindle and distaff for bow and arrows
paskuwatti-exchange-implements.description: After the crossing Paškuwatti removes the first implements and gives the man a bow and arrows.

paskuwatti-speak-exchange.title: Speak the change of implements
paskuwatti-speak-exchange.description: Paškuwatti’s words name the exchange of gendered implements.

paskuwatti-entreat-uliliyassi.title: Entreat Uliliyašši for the man
paskuwatti-entreat-uliliyassi.description: Paškuwatti asks Uliliyašši to come to the man and help him have descendants.

paskuwatti-return-and-set-table.title: Place the offering on a new table
paskuwatti-return-and-set-table.description: The offering is brought home and set on a new table.

zarpiya-take-implements.title: Take up the ritual implements
zarpiya-take-implements.description: The attendants gather the ritual implements before the door is closed.

zarpiya-close-door.title: Close the courtyard door
zarpiya-close-door.description: The master of the house closes the door.

zarpiya-anoint-door.title: Anoint the door with fine oil
zarpiya-anoint-door.description: Fine oil is applied to the closed door.

zarpiya-speak-threshold.title: Speak the closing formula
zarpiya-speak-threshold.description: The words ask that evil remain outside and good stay inside.

maddunani-take-provisions.title: Take two puppies, a piglet and provisions
maddunani-take-provisions.description: The augur takes two puppies, a piglet, breads, grain, cups and wine.

maddunani-prepare-at-night.title: Prepare the provisions at night
maddunani-prepare-at-night.description: The materials are prepared at night.

maddunani-move-through-camp.title: Move through the army camp at dawn
maddunani-move-through-camp.description: At daybreak the augur and an older man move through the army camp.

maddunani-speak-in-camp.title: Speak during the passage
maddunani-speak-in-camp.description: The augur and older man speak as they pass through the camp; the surviving words are damaged.

maddunani-watch-bird-omens.title: Watch birds at the beginning and end
maddunani-watch-bird-omens.description: Bird movements are read as omens as the rite begins and ends.

zelliya-take-funerary-goods.title: Take clothing and other goods
zelliya-take-funerary-goods.description: Zelliya lists garments, furniture, metals, vessels, food and drink for the dead.

zelliya-prepare-funerary-goods.title: Prepare the goods
zelliya-prepare-funerary-goods.description: The listed goods are prepared for the rite.

zelliya-carry-dead-outside.title: Carry the dead person outside
zelliya-carry-dead-outside.description: After a damaged passage, the dead person is carried outside.

zelliya-cremate-dead.title: Burn the dead person
zelliya-cremate-dead.description: The body is burned after being carried outside.

cmawro-string-stones.title: String the stones on flax
cmawro-string-stones.description: String the stones named earlier in the prescription on flax thread or cord.

cmawro-pack-ingredients-in-wool.title: Pack the named ingredients in wool
cmawro-pack-ingredients-in-wool.description: Place the named ingredients among the stones and wrap them in wool.

cmawro-wrap-in-leather.title: Wrap the bundle in leather
cmawro-wrap-in-leather.description: Wrap the prepared bundle in a leather pouch or covering.

cmawro-interlace-bundle.title: Interlace bundle and stones
cmawro-interlace-bundle.description: String the wrapped ingredients with the stones and wind the ingredients between them.

cmawro-place-around-neck.title: Place the amulet around the neck
cmawro-place-around-neck.description: Place the assembled amulet around the affected person's neck.

tapalazunauli-bring-donkey.title: Bring forward a donkey
tapalazunauli-bring-donkey.description: They bring a donkey forward for the rite.

tapalazunauli-assign-evil.title: Tell the donkey to carry away evil
tapalazunauli-assign-evil.description: The spoken words assign the evil to the donkey as its burden.

tapalazunauli-send-donkey.title: Drive the donkey toward enemy land
tapalazunauli-send-donkey.description: The donkey is driven away toward the enemy lands.

tapalazunauli-scatter-straw.title: Scatter a little straw
tapalazunauli-scatter-straw.description: Straw is scattered opposite the ritual place.

tapalazunauli-break-bread.title: Break a little bread
tapalazunauli-break-bread.description: A small amount of bread is broken opposite.

tapalazunauli-fill-basket.title: Put the materials in a basket
tapalazunauli-fill-basket.description: At evening the prepared materials are poured into a basket.

tapalazunauli-chant-at-gate.title: Chant at the gate
tapalazunauli-chant-at-gate.description: A woman chants while the basket is being carried out.

tapalazunauli-carry-basket-out.title: Carry the basket out
tapalazunauli-carry-basket-out.description: The prepared basket is carried across the boundary and away.

tapalazunauli-speak-to-god.title: Speak of food for the god and his dogs
tapalazunauli-speak-to-god.description: The speaker says fodder and food have been brought for the god and his dogs.

ummaya-prepare-at-wall.title: Prepare at the city wall
ummaya-prepare-at-wall.description: The rite is prepared at the city wall.

ummaya-conjure-on-ground.title: Conjure over the ground object
ummaya-conjure-on-ground.description: Ummaya conjures over an object on the ground; the object is not preserved in the passage.

ummaya-release-man.title: Release the man as a substitute
ummaya-release-man.description: A man is released as a substitute carrier after the incantation.

ummaya-release-oxen.title: Release two oxen as substitutes
ummaya-release-oxen.description: Two oxen are also released as substitute carriers.

cmawro-1-5-1-fashion-figures.title: Make figurines of the accused
cmawro-1-5-1-fashion-figures.description: Make wax figurines representing the warlock and witch.

cmawro-1-5-1-indict-figures.title: Indict the figures before Šamaš
cmawro-1-5-1-indict-figures.description: Bring the figures before Šamaš and indict those they represent.

cmawro-1-5-1-coat-figures.title: Coat the figures with tallow
cmawro-1-5-1-coat-figures.description: Apply tallow to the prepared figurines.

cmawro-1-5-1-pot-figures.title: Put the figures in a disposable pot
cmawro-1-5-1-pot-figures.description: Place the coated figures into a disposable clay pot.

cmawro-1-5-1-burn-figures.title: Burn the figures in the pot
cmawro-1-5-1-burn-figures.description: Burn the prepared figurines in the disposable pot.

cmawro-1-5-1-recite-return.title: Ask Šamaš to return the sorcery
cmawro-1-5-1-recite-return.description: Speak the appeal that the accused persons’ sorcery return to them; a variant prescribes three recitations.

cmawro-1-5-1-river-disposal.title: Throw the remains into the river
cmawro-1-5-1-river-disposal.description: Throw the disposable pot and burnt material into the river; a variant instead names the figurines.

cmawro-8-18-fashion-figures.title: Make figures from five materials
cmawro-8-18-fashion-figures.description: Fashion representations of warlock and witch from clay, dough, tallow, bitumen and wax.

cmawro-8-18-constrain-figures.title: Constrain the figures
cmawro-8-18-constrain-figures.description: Position the figures’ limbs in a constrained posture as the damaged instruction describes.

cmawro-8-18-pot-figures.title: Put the figures in a disposable pot
cmawro-8-18-pot-figures.description: Place the prepared figures in a disposable pot.

cmawro-8-18-juniper-censer.title: Set a juniper censer before Utu
cmawro-8-18-juniper-censer.description: Set a censer with juniper before the sun god Utu.

cmawro-8-18-grape-libation.title: Pour out grape must
cmawro-8-18-grape-libation.description: The affected person pours grape must as an offering.

cmawro-8-18-crush-figures.title: Crush the clay and dough figures
cmawro-8-18-crush-figures.description: Crush the clay and dough figures with a foot.

cmawro-8-18-burn-figures.title: Burn the tallow, wax and bitumen figures
cmawro-8-18-burn-figures.description: Burn the remaining combustible figures in fire.

cmawro-8-18-chew-plants.title: Chew the named plants and woods
cmawro-8-18-chew-plants.description: Chew tamarisk, innuš-soapwort, palm shoot, šulḫi-reed, wood-of-release and white cedar.

tunnawiya-royal-list-afflictions.title: Name the afflictions of the patient
tunnawiya-royal-list-afflictions.description: A litany that names, one by one, the afflictions lodged in the patient's body.
tunnawiya-royal-list-afflictions.matchRule: A litany that names, one by one, the afflictions lodged in the patient's body.

tunnawiya-royal-list-tongues.title: Name the tongues of every kind of person
tunnawiya-royal-list-tongues.description: A litany naming the 'tongues' (slander or curses) of many classes of people as harms to be removed.
tunnawiya-royal-list-tongues.matchRule: A litany naming the 'tongues' (slander or curses) of many classes of people as harms to be removed.

tunnawiya-royal-recount-causes.title: Recount how the harm was picked up
tunnawiya-royal-recount-causes.description: An utterance listing the possible routes (road, eyes, foot) by which the patient contracted harm.
tunnawiya-royal-recount-causes.matchRule: An utterance listing the possible routes (road, eyes, foot) by which the patient contracted harm.

tunnawiya-royal-name-evil-speech.title: Name the patient's evil speech against the gods
tunnawiya-royal-name-evil-speech.description: An utterance naming the patient's own offence (evil speech against the gods) among the causes of harm.
tunnawiya-royal-name-evil-speech.matchRule: An utterance naming the patient's own offence (evil speech against the gods) among the causes of harm.

tunnawiya-royal-fit-limbs.title: Fit the twelve limbs together
tunnawiya-royal-fit-limbs.description: A litany declaring each of the twelve limbs 'fitted' to its counterpart.
tunnawiya-royal-fit-limbs.matchRule: A litany declaring each of the twelve limbs 'fitted' to its counterpart.

tunnawiya-royal-cut-ram-limbs.title: Cut up the ram's twelve limbs
tunnawiya-royal-cut-ram-limbs.description: A ram's body is divided into twelve limbs to match the patient's twelve limbs.
tunnawiya-royal-cut-ram-limbs.matchRule: A ram's body is divided into twelve limbs to match the patient's twelve limbs.

tunnawiya-royal-limbs-take-sickness.description: An utterance by which each limb of a divided animal takes up the sickness of the same limb of the patient.
tunnawiya-royal-limbs-take-sickness.matchRule: An utterance by which each limb of a divided animal takes up the sickness of the same limb of the patient.

tunnawiya-royal-declare-pulled-out.description: A first-person statement that the practitioner has pulled the harm out of the patient.

tunnawiya-royal-conjure-round-limbs.title: Conjure around the twelve limbs

tunnawiya-royal-hold-over-back.title: Hold it over his back
tunnawiya-royal-hold-over-back.description: An unnamed object is held over the patient's back after he lies down in a new position.
tunnawiya-royal-hold-over-back.matchRule: An unnamed object is held over the patient's back after he lies down in a new position.

tunnawiya-royal-plough-analogy.title: Compare the patient to a field ploughed again
tunnawiya-royal-plough-analogy.description: An analogy between re-ploughing a field and repeating the treatment on the patient.
tunnawiya-royal-plough-analogy.matchRule: An analogy between re-ploughing a field and repeating the treatment on the patient.

tunnawiya-royal-spit-into-mouth.title: Spit into the sheep's mouth
tunnawiya-royal-spit-into-mouth.description: The patient spits into the mouth of an animal carrier held out to him.
tunnawiya-royal-spit-into-mouth.matchRule: The patient spits into the mouth of an animal carrier held out to him.

tunnawiya-royal-command-spit-out.title: Command him to spit out the harms
tunnawiya-royal-command-spit-out.description: A spoken command that the patient spit out named harms.
tunnawiya-royal-command-spit-out.matchRule: A spoken command that the patient spit out named harms.

tunnawiya-royal-bring-piglets.title: Bring a dough piglet and a live piglet
tunnawiya-royal-bring-piglets.description: A live animal and a dough model of the same animal are brought together.
tunnawiya-royal-bring-piglets.matchRule: A live animal and a dough model of the same animal are brought together.

tunnawiya-royal-swing-live-piglet.title: Swing the live piglet away
tunnawiya-royal-swing-live-piglet.description: A live piglet is swung repeatedly (away from the patient?).
tunnawiya-royal-swing-live-piglet.matchRule: A live piglet is swung repeatedly (away from the patient?).

tunnawiya-royal-hold-dough-piglet.title: Hold the dough piglet close to him
tunnawiya-royal-hold-dough-piglet.description: A dough model animal is held close to the patient as a carrier.
tunnawiya-royal-hold-dough-piglet.matchRule: A dough model animal is held close to the patient as a carrier.

tunnawiya-royal-great-god-historiola.title: Tell of the great god driving from Landa
tunnawiya-royal-great-god-historiola.description: A narrated myth of a god's journey spoken over the patient.
tunnawiya-royal-great-god-historiola.matchRule: A narrated myth of a god's journey spoken over the patient.

tunnawiya-royal-speak-patient-name.title: Speak the patient's name
tunnawiya-royal-speak-patient-name.description: The practitioner inserts the patient's name into the incantation.
tunnawiya-royal-speak-patient-name.matchRule: The practitioner inserts the patient's name into the incantation.

tunnawiya-royal-search-historiola.title: Tell of the gods' search of his body
tunnawiya-royal-search-historiola.description: A narrated myth in which gods search the patient's body part by part.
tunnawiya-royal-search-historiola.matchRule: A narrated myth in which gods search the patient's body part by part.

tunnawiya-royal-cut-them-off.title: Cut them off from the limbs
tunnawiya-royal-cut-them-off.description: A spoken command, within a myth, to cut harms off from the patient's body parts.
tunnawiya-royal-cut-them-off.matchRule: A spoken command, within a myth, to cut harms off from the patient's body parts.

tunnawiya-royal-remove-litany.title: Let her remove the tongues
tunnawiya-royal-remove-litany.description: A litany asking a goddess to remove each named harm in turn.
tunnawiya-royal-remove-litany.matchRule: A litany asking a goddess to remove each named harm in turn.

mursili-plague-prayer-inquire-egypt-oath.title: Put the Egyptian oath-breach to an oracle
mursili-plague-prayer-inquire-egypt-oath.description: Having found the old tablet about Egypt, the king makes the matter of the broken oath the subject of an oracle inquiry.
mursili-plague-prayer-inquire-egypt-oath.matchRule: A king submits a found cause of divine anger to oracle inquiry.

mursili-plague-prayer-inquire-mala-offer.title: Put the neglected Mala offering to an oracle
mursili-plague-prayer-inquire-mala-offer.description: The king also asks the oracle about the long-neglected offering to the river Mala; it confirms he must stand before the Storm-god.
mursili-plague-prayer-inquire-mala-offer.matchRule: Oracle inquiry into a neglected cult offering.

mursili-plague-prayer-confess-sin.title: Confess the sin
mursili-plague-prayer-confess-sin.description: Before the Storm-god the king acknowledges the sin: 'it is so, we did it.'
mursili-plague-prayer-confess-sin.matchRule: A first-person confession of a specific offence to the god it angered.

mursili-plague-prayer-vow-mala-offering.title: Vow to perform the Mala offering
mursili-plague-prayer-vow-mala-offering.description: The king undertakes to see to the river Mala offering, and asks that the plague be put right.
mursili-plague-prayer-vow-mala-offering.matchRule: A promise to resume a neglected offering.

mursili-plague-prayer-confess-fathers-si.title: Confess the father's sin
mursili-plague-prayer-confess-fathers-si.description: The king explains that a father's sin reaches his son and confesses Šuppiluliuma's transgression before the Storm-god and the gods.

mursili-plague-prayer-soothe-and-send-aw.title: Ask the god's soul to be soothed and the plague sent away
mursili-plague-prayer-soothe-and-send-aw.description: Because the sin is confessed, the king asks that the soul of the Storm-god and the gods be soothed, that they have pity, and send the plague away.
mursili-plague-prayer-soothe-and-send-aw.matchRule: Request that a god's anger be soothed after confession.

mursili-plague-prayer-hear-me.title: Call on the Storm-god to hear and keep him alive
mursili-plague-prayer-hear-me.description: The king announces his plea about the plague and calls on the Storm-god to hear him and keep him alive.
mursili-plague-prayer-hear-me.matchRule: Direct invocation of a named god to hear a plea.

mursili-plague-prayer-bird-and-servant.title: Argue by the bird and the servant
mursili-plague-prayer-bird-and-servant.description: The king offers comparisons: a bird kept alive in its nest, a servant whose lord hears his plea, a servant forgiven because he confessed.
mursili-plague-prayer-bird-and-servant.matchRule: Rhetorical analogy of lord and servant addressed to a god.

mursili-plague-prayer-offer-compensation.title: Offer further compensation
mursili-plague-prayer-offer-compensation.description: The king argues the land has already paid twentyfold through the plague, yet undertakes to give any further compensation the god reveals in a dream.
mursili-plague-prayer-offer-compensation.matchRule: Promise of restitution to an offended god on revelation.

mursili-plague-prayer-spare-cult-personn.title: Ask that the remaining cult personnel die no more
mursili-plague-prayer-spare-cult-personn.description: While he sets the matter right, the king asks that the surviving bread-offerers and libation-pourers die no more.
mursili-plague-prayer-spare-cult-personn.matchRule: Plea that those who feed the gods be spared.

mursili-plague-prayer-reveal-other-cause.title: Ask for any other cause to be revealed
mursili-plague-prayer-reveal-other-cause.description: If people die for another reason, the king asks to see it in a dream, by oracle, or through a man of god.
mursili-plague-prayer-reveal-other-cause.matchRule: Request for divine disclosure through dream, oracle or prophet.

mursili-plague-prayer-order-pure-sleep.title: Order the priests to sleep in purity
mursili-plague-prayer-order-pure-sleep.description: The king has ordered all (probably priests) to sleep regularly in purity, apparently to receive dreams.
mursili-plague-prayer-order-pure-sleep.matchRule: Ordered sleep in a state of purity to receive a dream.

army-ritual-hot-stone.title: Speak the analogy of the hot stone
army-ritual-hot-stone.description: As a hot stone falls silent in water, so may the addressee's battle grow cold.
army-ritual-hot-stone.matchRule: Spoken analogy by which a hot stone cooling in water quells hostility.

army-ritual-winter-torpor.title: Bind the rivals by the torpor of winter
army-ritual-winter-torpor.description: As winter's torpor seizes, so may the spells likewise seize the speaker's rivals.
army-ritual-winter-torpor.matchRule: Spoken binding of enemies by a seasonal analogy.

army-ritual-mighty-troops.title: Pray that the troops be mighty
army-ritual-mighty-troops.description: The speaker asks that his troops be mighty.
army-ritual-mighty-troops.matchRule: Petition for the strength of one's own army.

army-ritual-father-gods-protect.title: Ask the father-gods to protect the son
army-ritual-father-gods-protect.description: The speaker asks the father-gods to protect the son, young and grown, and rejoice in his life.
army-ritual-father-gods-protect.matchRule: Petition to ancestral gods for protection of a named person.

army-ritual-gods-on-our-side.title: Declare the gods are on our side
army-ritual-gods-on-our-side.description: The speaker declares that the gods have stepped to their side and the kings have spoken for them.
army-ritual-gods-on-our-side.matchRule: Declaration of divine alignment with one's party.

army-ritual-hasten-troops.title: Ask that the troops be hastened
army-ritual-hasten-troops.description: Great and small together are asked to hasten the troops along.
army-ritual-hasten-troops.matchRule: Petition that one's troops move swiftly.

lapana-plague-bull.title: Provide a bull
lapana-plague-bull.description: One bull is listed among the materials.
lapana-plague-bull.matchRule: Provision of a bull for a plague rite (fate unstated).

lapana-plague-wicker-tables.title: Set out four wicker tables
lapana-plague-wicker-tables.description: Four wicker tables are listed, apparently for the lord of the city.

lapana-plague-evening-fire.title: Kindle a fire in the evening
lapana-plague-evening-fire.description: When evening comes they go and kindle a fire.
lapana-plague-evening-fire.matchRule: Kindling a fire for an evening offering.

lapana-plague-raw-cooked.title: Offer raw and cooked portions to the gods
lapana-plague-raw-cooked.description: They offer to the gods and set raw and cooked portions on the ground.
lapana-plague-raw-cooked.matchRule: Offering raw and cooked portions together.

lapana-plague-burn.title: Burn the offering
lapana-plague-burn.description: The passage closes with burning; the object is lost.
lapana-plague-burn.matchRule: Burning at the close of an offering (object unknown).

lapana-plague-bow.title: Bow down to the gods
lapana-plague-bow.description: They bow down to the gods.
lapana-plague-bow.matchRule: Prostration before gods at a plague rite.

lapana-plague-in-mouth.title: Place a little in the mouth, three times
lapana-plague-in-mouth.description: A little of something is placed in the mouth; the act is repeated three times.
lapana-plague-in-mouth.matchRule: Placing a small portion in the mouth, repeated thrice.

libu-mix-urine-clay.title: Mix donkey urine with school clay
libu-mix-urine-clay.description: Mix the urine of a living donkey with clay from the tablet-house.
libu-mix-urine-clay.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-make-donkeys.title: Knead and make two clay donkeys
libu-make-donkeys.description: Knead the mixture and fashion two donkey figurines.
libu-make-donkeys.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-attach-strap-tail.title: Attach the strap and tail-hair to the figurine
libu-attach-strap-tail.description: Put the living donkey's harness-strap on the figurine's strap and its tail-hair on the figurine's tail.
libu-attach-strap-tail.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-make-substitute.title: Make the substitute from the patient's urine, hair and nails
libu-make-substitute.description: Mix the patient's urine, armpit and chest hair and nail-parings into the clay and fashion the substitute figure.
libu-make-substitute.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-dress-mount-substitute.title: Clothe the substitute and set it on the donkey
libu-dress-mount-substitute.description: Clothe the substitute figure, put a headdress on it and set it riding on the DÚSU-donkey.
libu-dress-mount-substitute.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-load-sacks.title: Load sacks on the two leading donkeys
libu-load-sacks.description: Fill a sack and set it on the first donkey; set a sack full of flour on the second.
libu-load-sacks.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-make-driver.title: Make a clay driver with a goad
libu-make-driver.description: Make another clay figure, clothe it, put a wooden ŠU.KIN (a goad?) in its hand and station it behind the donkeys.
libu-make-driver.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-bring-to-roof.title: Bring the figures up onto the roof before Šamaš
libu-bring-to-roof.description: Station the substitute with the donkeys and bring the donkey figures up onto the roof before Šamaš.
libu-bring-to-roof.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-strew-offering.title: Strew flour, dates and mashatu-flour before Šamaš
libu-strew-offering.description: Strew flour, dates and mashatu-flour as a strewn offering.
libu-strew-offering.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-address-samas.title: Address Šamaš as lord of judgment
libu-address-samas.description: The exorcist addresses Šamaš as judge and names the patient whom li'bu has seized without his knowing.
libu-address-samas.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-carry-substitute-out.title: Bring the substitute down and out to the open country
libu-carry-substitute-out.description: Bring the figures down from the roof and take the substitute out to the open country.
libu-carry-substitute-out.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-patient-gives-libu.title: The patient hands li'bu to his substitute
libu-patient-gives-libu.description: The patient tells li'bu that he gives it to his substitute and orders it to be gone.
libu-patient-gives-libu.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-donkeys-in-basket.title: Place the donkey figures in a basket before Šamaš
libu-donkeys-in-basket.description: Place the donkey figures in a basket before Šamaš.
libu-donkeys-in-basket.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-pour-seven-sila.title: Pour out seven sila each of flour, dates and oil
libu-pour-seven-sila.description: Pour seven sila each of flour, mashatu-flour, dates and oil on the ground.
libu-pour-seven-sila.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-address-nisaba.title: Invoke Nisaba and drive out the curse
libu-address-nisaba.description: The patient invokes Nisaba, who releases the curse, and declares the evil adjured and driven out.
libu-address-nisaba.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-draw-design-adjure.title: Draw a design and adjure the evil by the gods
libu-draw-design-adjure.description: Draw a design and adjure the evil by Enlil, Ninlil, Asalluḫi, Baba and Ningišzida to be led out, chased and gone, never to return.
libu-draw-design-adjure.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-strew-at-esegu.title: Take it out to the ešegu-bush and strew flour and dates
libu-strew-at-esegu.description: Take it out of the house to the open country and at the ešegu-thornbush strew coarse flour, dates and mashatu-flour.
libu-strew-at-esegu.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-station-weapons.title: Station donkeys and weapons before Šamaš
libu-station-weapons.description: Behind the offering station two donkeys before Šamaš, a weapon behind the donkeys, and a weapon behind the donkey ridden by the substitute.
libu-station-weapons.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-address-samas-oath.title: Address Šamaš, list the seizing demons and lay the oath
libu-address-samas-oath.description: Invoke Šamaš as judge, list the ghosts and demons that have seized the patient, and declare that the oath of the great gods has been put in his mouth.
libu-address-samas-oath.matchRule: Match only an address to Šamaš as judge that names the seizing agents and declares the oath.

libu-address-esegu.title: Seize the ešegu-bush and bid it plead with Šamaš
libu-address-esegu.description: Tell the ešegu, offspring of Enlil, that it has been seized on the patient's account, bid it plead with Šamaš, and promise its release when li'bu lets the patient go.
libu-address-esegu.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-anoint-bind-esegu.title: Pour oil on the ešegu and bind it to a rush
libu-anoint-bind-esegu.description: Pour oil on the ešegu, bind it to a rush and wrap its top all round.
libu-anoint-bind-esegu.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-release-bargain.title: Ask Šamaš to free the patient from fever
libu-release-bargain.description: The exorcist asks the sun god Šamaš to make the illness release the patient. In return, he promises to release the thornbush used in the rite.
libu-release-bargain.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-place-loaves-designs.title: Draw designs and set a dried loaf at each
libu-place-loaves-designs.description: Draw two designs of a cubit and seven designs before the seven(?), and place a dried loaf wherever there is a design.
libu-place-loaves-designs.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-strew-city-gate.title: Throw flour at the city gate
libu-strew-city-gate.description: Entering the city gate, throw flour to either side and in the middle, and on both door-leaves.
libu-strew-city-gate.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-adjure-at-gate.title: Adjure the evil not to enter the door
libu-adjure-at-gate.description: Adjure the evil by the great gods of the ešegu not to enter the open door, and send it away.
libu-adjure-at-gate.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-mix-salt-cress.title: Mix salt and cress into the poured flour
libu-mix-salt-cress.description: Mix salt and cress into the flour poured out as offering.
libu-mix-salt-cress.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-crush-juniper.title: Crush juniper and mix it with oil
libu-crush-juniper.description: For a recurrent third-day fever, crush a sila of juniper and mix it with oil.
libu-crush-juniper.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

libu-recite-arabapura.title: Recite the incantation during treatment
libu-recite-arabapura.description: Recite the incantation '[A]rābapura'(?) during the treatment, repeating plant and incantation unchanged until the seizures leave.
libu-recite-arabapura.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

poultice-crush-plants.title: Crush the plants and mix them as one
poultice-crush-plants.description: Crush ḪA.AB-plant, Ú.RA.AN.NA, juniper, an aromatic and ninû-plant, and mix them together.
poultice-crush-plants.matchRule: Crushing of plant or aromatic ingredients for a poultice; distinguish crushing figures.

poultice-boil-mixture.title: Boil the mixture in kasû-juice
poultice-boil-mixture.description: Boil the crushed mixture in kasû-juice.
poultice-boil-mixture.matchRule: Boiling or decocting a poultice mixture in a liquid (juice, beer or wine).

poultice-bandage.title: Keep bandaging the patient
poultice-bandage.description: Keep bandaging the patient with the poultice.
poultice-bandage.matchRule: Applying a cooked poultice to the patient as a bandage.

poultice-mix-emmer.title: Mix the aromatics with emmer flour
poultice-mix-emmer.description: Mix the crushed aromatics together with emmer flour.
poultice-mix-emmer.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

poultice-mix-ghee-beer.title: Mix seeds with ghee and beer and bandage
poultice-mix-ghee-beer.description: Mix a long list of seeds and plants with ghee and in first-quality beer, then keep bandaging him.
poultice-mix-ghee-beer.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

poultice-perform-purification.title: Perform a purification for the sick man
poultice-perform-purification.description: Perform a purification (takpirtu) for the sick man, apparently with a ḫulduppû, bind him(?) and keep doing so for two or three months.
poultice-perform-purification.matchRule: Match only the same act on the same principal object.

cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-draw-circle-round.title: Draw a magic circle round the crucible
cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-draw-circle-round.description: A magic circle is drawn around the crucible.

cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-arrange-figures-i.title: Arrange figures of nine materials in the crucible
cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-arrange-figures-i.description: Figures of tamarisk, cedar, tallow, wax, husks, bitumen, gypsum, clay and dough are placed in order in the crucible.

cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-identify-figures-.title: Point at the figures and name them as the doer
cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-identify-figures-.description: Reciting the incantation "this effigy of the doer", the practitioner stretches a finger toward the figures.

cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-set-torch-on-fat-.title: Put a torch on the tallow and wax figures
cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-set-torch-on-fat-.description: With a further incantation, a torch is put on the tallow and wax figures.

cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-insert-woods-and-.title: Stick cedar, cypress, myrtle and reed into it
cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-insert-woods-and-.description: Cedar, cypress, myrtle(?) and good reed are stuck into its interior and something is sprinkled.

cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-light-torch-from-.title: Light the torch from sulphur fire and recite
cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-light-torch-from-.description: The torch is lit in a sulphur fire, and the incantation "I lift the torch" is recited.

cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-throw-fire-into-c.title: Throw fire into the crucible
cmawro-q002713-9-22-31-throw-fire-into-c.description: Fire is thrown into the crucible, burning the figures set in it.

cmawro-q004239-11-1-1-pound-paste.title: Pound sulphur, gypsum and red paste together
cmawro-q004239-11-1-1-pound-paste.description: Sulphur, gypsum and red paste are pounded together into a mixture.

cmawro-q004239-11-1-1-recite-tear-out-so.title: Recite "Furious, furious … tear out the sorcery"
cmawro-q004239-11-1-1-recite-tear-out-so.description: The incantation "Furious, furious, arisen evil …" ends with a command to tear out the sorcery.

cmawro-q004239-11-1-1-recite-into-paste-.title: Recite into the paste; apply it to the door-jamb
cmawro-q004239-11-1-1-recite-into-paste-.description: The incantation is recited three times into the mixture, which goes on the door-jamb of the man's house gate.

cmawro-q004239-11-1-1-wash-off-into-clot.title: Wash the paste off with silt into a cloth
cmawro-q004239-11-1-1-wash-off-into-clot.description: Afterwards the mixture is washed off with silt, into a cloth trimming, and the harm is released.

cmawro-q004239-11-1-1-wrap-sulphur-oil-i.title: Wrap sulphur and oil in combed fleece
cmawro-q004239-11-1-1-wrap-sulphur-oil-i.description: An alkaline plant, henbane(?) and a good mixture, with sulphur and oil, are enclosed in combed fleece.

cmawro-q004239-11-1-1-bury-at-gate-and-s.title: Bury it at the outer gate and door socket
cmawro-q004239-11-1-1-bury-at-gate-and-s.description: The fleece deposit is buried at the outer gate and at the door's pivot socket, so that the sorcery is lost and cannot come near the man and his house.

cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-sprinkle-riverbank.title: Sweep and sprinkle the riverbank
cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-sprinkle-riverbank.description: On a favourable day, at the riverbank, the ground is beaten (swept) and sprinkled with pure water.

cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-altar-and-libation.title: Set up an altar and pour a libation
cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-altar-and-libation.description: A portable altar is set up before the god and a libation is poured.

cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-make-male-female-c.title: Make a male and a female figure of clay
cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-make-male-female-c.description: Two figures, a male and a female, are made of clay.

cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-clothe-and-stand-b.title: The sick man dresses, stands before the god, recites
cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-clothe-and-stand-b.description: The sick man puts on a garment, stands before the god and recites the incantation three times.

cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-send-evil-across-r.title: Ask that the evil cross river and mountain
cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-send-evil-across-r.description: In the incantation the evil is told to cross over river and mountain and the sorcery to be far from the body.

cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-smoke-and-tamarisk.title: Like smoke, like uprooted tamarisk
cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-smoke-and-tamarisk.description: The incantation wishes the evil to rise like smoke to the sky and, like uprooted tamarisk, not return to its place.

cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-beer-libation-to-r.title: Pour beer before the river
cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-beer-libation-to-r.description: After reciting, he goes before the river and pours a beer libation.

cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-dip-in-river-three.title: Sink three times in the river in a textile
cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-dip-in-river-three.description: The sick man, with a textile, sinks into the river three times.

cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-ask-river-to-take-.title: Ask the river to carry the evil away
cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-ask-river-to-take-.description: In the incantation to the river he asks it to take away the evil and carry it down to the underground waters, so that it not come near him or his house.

cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-come-up-strip-and-.title: Come up, tear off the textile, bathe
cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-come-up-strip-and-.description: After three recitations he comes up, the textile is torn away, and he is bathed from a holy-water vessel while an incantation is recited; then another textile.

cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-touch-brewers-mash.title: Enter a brewer's house and touch the mash tub
cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-touch-brewers-mash.description: Purified with censer, torch and pure water, he goes along the street, enters a brewer's house and touches the stand and mash tub.

cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-touch-gate-gypsum-.title: Touch the gate with gypsum and bitumen
cmawro-q005109-11-3-1-touch-gate-gypsum-.description: The gate is touched with gypsum and bitumen; this concludes the apotropaic ritual.

potency-catch-partridge.title: Catch a male partridge
potency-catch-partridge.description: Catch a named live bird or animal as a remedy ingredient.
potency-catch-partridge.matchRule: Catch a live animal named as a remedy ingredient; record species and season on the occurrence.

potency-pluck-strangle.title: Pluck and strangle the partridge
potency-pluck-strangle.description: Pluck a bird and kill it for use as a remedy ingredient.
potency-pluck-strangle.matchRule: Pluck and kill a bird whose body becomes a remedy ingredient, not an offering.

potency-salt-dry.title: Salt and dry the bird
potency-salt-dry.description: Salt or smear an ingredient and dry it.
potency-salt-dry.matchRule: Salt and dry a remedy ingredient before crushing.

potency-crush-with-thorn.title: Crush with thorn seed
potency-crush-with-thorn.description: Crush dried ingredients together into a powder.
potency-crush-with-thorn.matchRule: Crush named dried ingredients for a remedy.

potency-drink-in-beer.title: Give it to drink in beer
potency-drink-in-beer.description: Give a crushed remedy to the patient to drink in a named liquid.
potency-drink-in-beer.matchRule: Give a prepared remedy to the patient to drink; record the liquid (beer, water, wine) on the occurrence.

potency-blood-into-water.title: Let the blood fall into water
potency-blood-into-water.description: Let the blood of an animal fall into water to make a remedy.
potency-blood-into-water.matchRule: Drain animal blood into water as a remedy base.

potency-wrap-in-wool.title: Wrap in wool
potency-wrap-in-wool.description: Wrap remedy ingredients in wool as a bundle to be worn or placed.
potency-wrap-in-wool.matchRule: Wrap remedy ingredients in wool; record the source of the wool.

potency-smear-salt-plant.title: Smear with salt and nīnû-plant
potency-smear-salt-plant.description: Smear a bird with salt and a named plant before drying.
potency-smear-salt-plant.matchRule: Smear an ingredient with salt and a plant before drying it.

potency-mix-roasted-flour.title: Mix with roasted-grain flour
potency-mix-roasted-flour.description: Mix a crushed ingredient with flour.
potency-mix-roasted-flour.matchRule: Mix a crushed remedy ingredient with a named flour.

potency-form-pellets.title: Form pellets
potency-form-pellets.description: Crush ingredients, mix with flour and shape into pellets.
potency-form-pellets.matchRule: Shape a crushed remedy mixture into pellets.

potency-bind-on-hips.title: Bind on the hips
potency-bind-on-hips.description: Tie a remedy bundle on the patient’s body.
potency-bind-on-hips.matchRule: Tie or bind a prepared bundle onto a named part of the patient’s body.

potency-rinse-body.title: Rinse with water and kasû
potency-rinse-body.description: Rinse the patient’s body with water and a plant.
potency-rinse-body.matchRule: Rinse the patient’s whole body with a named liquid and plant.

potency-anoint-oil.title: Anoint repeatedly with oil
potency-anoint-oil.description: Rub oil containing a remedy onto the patient.
potency-anoint-oil.matchRule: Anoint the patient with a named oil or remedy.

potency-sumerian-incantation.title: Recite the Sumerian incantation
potency-sumerian-incantation.description: Recite a prescribed incantation as part of a medical prescription.
potency-sumerian-incantation.matchRule: Recite an incantation belonging to a medical prescription.

potency-crush-decoct-sinews.title: Crush and decoct the sinews
potency-crush-decoct-sinews.description: Crush animal parts between stones and boil them down.
potency-crush-decoct-sinews.matchRule: Crush remedy ingredients and decoct them.

remedies-take-herbs.title: Take the herbs
remedies-take-herbs.description: Take named plants as ingredients of a remedy.
remedies-take-herbs.matchRule: Take named plants for a remedy; record the plants on the occurrence.

remedies-give-seven-days.title: Give the herbs for seven days
remedies-give-seven-days.description: Give a prepared remedy to the patient over a stated number of days.
remedies-give-seven-days.matchRule: Give a remedy to the patient over several days; record the duration and timing.

remedies-steep-sift.title: Steep and sift the bulbs
remedies-steep-sift.description: Steep ingredients in a liquid and sift them.
remedies-steep-sift.matchRule: Steep remedy ingredients in liquid and sift or strain them.

remedies-sew-into-cord.title: Sew into a cord from a leopard’s kill
remedies-sew-into-cord.description: Sew a remedy ingredient into a cord or strip of leather.
remedies-sew-into-cord.matchRule: Sew or enclose an ingredient in a leather cord; record the source animal.

remedies-twist-sinew.title: Twist in the sinew
remedies-twist-sinew.description: Twist an animal sinew into a cord.
remedies-twist-sinew.matchRule: Twist a sinew into a cord or amulet.

remedies-heat-compress.title: Heat and apply a compress
remedies-heat-compress.description: Heat a compress and apply it to the patient.
remedies-heat-compress.matchRule: Heat a compress or pad and apply it to the patient.

remedies-crush-into-bag.title: Crush the plants into a bag
remedies-crush-into-bag.description: Crush plants and store them in a bag.
remedies-crush-into-bag.matchRule: Crush remedy plants; record any container.

remedies-carry-into-house.title: Carry it into the house
remedies-carry-into-house.description: Carry a remedy indoors after exposure.
remedies-carry-into-house.matchRule: Carry a prepared remedy into a building.

remedies-into-honey.title: Give it in honey until he recovers
remedies-into-honey.description: Mix a remedy into honey and give it to the patient.

remedies-gut-fish.title: Gut a fish
remedies-gut-fish.description: Take a fish and remove its inner parts for a remedy.
remedies-gut-fish.matchRule: Gut a fish as a remedy ingredient.

expose-remedy-to-stars.title: Leave a remedy out under the stars
expose-remedy-to-stars.description: A prepared remedy is left outdoors overnight, under the stars, before it is given.
expose-remedy-to-stars.matchRule: A prepared remedy is set outdoors overnight and the text names the night or the stars. KUB 4.48 (Babylonian, copied at Ḫattuša) leaves blood-water out overnight; KUB 44.64 (Hittite, CTH 461) leaves a bag of crushed plants out "for the stars". Liquid and container differ and remain on each occurrence; the shared act is overnight exposure of a remedy.
